newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Syria wins Tunisia's support on Mideast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Syria wins Tunisia's support on Mideast peace talks.

text.p: Syria said on Wednesday it had won Tunisian backing for its demand that Israel's current government must honour offers made in peace negotiations by its previous leadership.

Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam made the statement after meeting Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali as part of a tour of North African countries to build support. Tunisian officials confirmed the position.

"I reaffirmed to President Ben Ali that Syria was ready to resume talks from the point they were suspended and once the Israeli government will approve the commitments made by the previous Israeli government," he said.
"President Ben Ali asked me to carry to President Hafez al-)Assad a message reiterating Tunisia's support for Syria in its efforts for resuming the peace negotiations," he added.

Damascus says when Israel suspended the talks a year ago, the two countries were on the verge of an agreement based on the Israel Labour government's private commitment to withdraw from the Golan Heights.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who defeated the Labour leader in elections in May, rejects the principle of returning land for peace and insists on keeping the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in 1967.
Before visiting Tunis, Khaddam was in Libya on Tuesday and Morocco on Monday.
